exposure: HIV diagnosis timing (before pregnancy, during pregnancy, during delivery)
cohort: 15 infants born to HIV-positive mothers between 2009 and 2019 at a single hospital.
finding: The study found that perinatal transmission of HIV can be reduced through interventions before, during, and after birth, highlighting the importance of early HIV diagnosis and specialized care for pregnant women with HIV.
mod_finding: Out of 2 infants born via spontaneous vaginal delivery, one received zidovudine prophylaxis and remained HIV negative, while the other was taken by the mother without permission and their HIV status is unknown.
gest_age: 38 weeks (for one infant with positive HIV viral load)
